data.title: Radio
data.tagline: Choose exactly one option from a small set
data.description: Radio buttons show mutually exclusive choices such as payment method or visibility. Give the group a clear question and keep all options visible. If there are many options or users need to search, a Select may work better.

use: Any short list with one valid answer
avoid: Use it when several options may be selected
Hide a long list of choices in a crowded group
Use labels that do not explain the difference
Offer no way to clear the choice when “none” is valid

lessonPractice.title: Pickup offers four time slots. People must choose one and should compare every option at a glance. What fits best?

options.label: Show a radio group where a new choice clears the previous one
options.feedback: A small mutually exclusive set fits a visible radio group, letting people compare every slot.

options.label: Show checkboxes and reject multiple choices only on submit
options.feedback: Checkboxes communicate multiple selection, so their meaning would conflict with the actual rule.

options.label: Put the slots in a dropdown that opens into a list
options.feedback: A dropdown saves space, but it works against the stated need to see and compare all four options.

data.agentPrompt: Show the four pickup slots as one visible radio group with exactly one choice. Verify clicking labels, keyboard changes, and selecting a new slot clearing the previous one.
